p: Anglia Parkway South sits on the north-western side of Ipswich, close to the A14, so it's an easy trip in from across Suffolk without battling the town centre. Once you've parked up and bounced out, you're well placed for a few other Ipswich favourites.

The town has serious history. Cardinal Wolsey, Henry VIII's powerful right-hand man, was born in Ipswich, and the medieval streets around the Buttermarket still show off the Ancient House, famous for its incredibly detailed decorative plasterwork, known as pargeting. It's free to look at from the street and well worth pointing out to the kids.
Football families will know Portman Road, home of Ipswich Town, which brings a big crowd into the centre on match days. If you'd rather avoid the rush, check the fixtures before you travel.

For outdoor space beyond Christchurch Park, Holywells Park on the east side has woodland, ponds and a play area, and Orwell Country Park runs along the river near the famous Orwell Bridge. South of town, Jimmy's Farm and Wildlife Park at Wherstead is a big family favourite with animals, trails and a farm shop.

Fancy the seaside? Felixstowe is a short drive down the A14, with its long promenade and beach, and makes a cracking second stop on a dry day. All told, Ipswich makes a better base for a weekend than many people expect.
One more for the list: the Waterfront marina is home to the old maltings and quayside buildings, and on a fine evening it's a lovely spot to sit by the boats with a bite to eat before heading home.
